FOREWORD

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 November 1982, after the draft finalized by Wrought Steel Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council.

0.2 This standard has been prepared with a view to guiding the manufacturers and users of tinplate and to assist them in the unified interpretation of common terms used in the trade.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard reduced tinplate definitions.
2. TERMS covers a list of general trade and cold-reduced blackplate terms relating to coldtheir together with

AND

DEFINITIONS

2.1 Steel Types 2.1.1 Stabilized ( Also Known as Type D ) - Low carbon steel fully deoxidisetl by addition of suitable deoxidant, for example, aluminium. This type of steel possesses virtually no strain-ageing characteristics.
2.1.2 Rimmed Steel ( Non-stabilized ) - Low carbon steels that are not This type of steel is prone to flutting and deoxidised by some deoxidant. ageing. 2.1.3 Nitrogenized -. Steel containing a controlled amount of nitrogen customarily introduced during the steel making process as strengthening It may be used for the high tinplate tempers, and hardening element.

IS:10340-1982 2.2 Plate Types 2.2.1 Cold-Reduced produced continuous strip/sheet. Blackplate - Low or semi-continuous carbon mild steel strip/sheet cold-reduction of hot-rolled steel low hot-dip carbon tinning

2.2.2 Cold-Reduced Hot-Dipped Tinplate - Cold-reduced mild steel strip/sheet which has been tinned by the process. 2.2.3 Cold-Reduced Electrolytic Tinplate reduced strip/sheet which has been tinned 2.3 Annealing Types of cold-reduced

Low carbon mild steel coldby the electrolytic process.

2.3.1 Batch Annealing - Annealing within a protective atmosphere.

2.3.2 Continuous Annealing - Annealing of cold-reduced strip in a single thickness within a protective atmosphere. This produces relatively stiffer product which exhibits a finer grain size than batch annealed material. 2.4 Post Plating Surface Treatments

2.4.1 Flow Brightening - Process used to produce a bright tin coating from the silvery white as plate deposit by rapid melting of tin under controlled conditions of heating and quenching. 2.4.2 Passiuation - Chemical electrolytic tinplate to produce ance to surface discolouration properties. or electrochemical treatment applied to a stabilized surface of improved resistand superior lacquering and lithographic

2.4.3 Oiling - Application of a very thin uniform oil film ( generally dioctyl sebacate ) to the surface of electrolytic tinplate by passage through the oil. of a very thin uniform oil film 2.4.4 Oiling-Electrostatic - Application ( generally dioctyl sebacate ) to the surface of electrolytic tinplate by electrostatic deposition of fine oil particles from a mist. 2.5 Grades

2.5.1 Blackplate which at the time of 2.5.1.1 First grade ( prime ) - Blackplates Under despatch are free from defects readily visible to the unaided eye. normal conditions of storage and use, they are suitable for lacquering and printing over the whole surface. 4

IS : 10340- 1982 2.5.1.2 Second grade - Seconds is the grade designation given to blackplates which at the time of despatch have a minimum of 75 percent of usable area.
2.5.1.3 Unassorted ( grade standard ) - Unassorted ( UA ) is the grade designation given to blackplates, normally produced in line using usual These contain primes and inspection and classification procedures. seconds. The quality of seconds may be up to 15 percent at the time of despatch. 2.5.2 Hot Dipped Tinplate

2.5.2.1 First ( grade prime ) - Tinplates which at the time of despatch Under normal are free from defects readily visible to the unaided eye. for lacquering and conditions of storage and use, they are suitable printing over the whole surface of the sheet. 2.5.2.2 Second grade - Seconds is the grade designation given to hotdipped tinplates which at the time of despatch have a minimum of 75 percent of usable area. 2.5.3 Electrolytic Tinplate ( Equalb OY Di$eerentialQ Coated )

2.5.3.1 First ( grade prime ) - Tinplates which at the time of despatch Under normal are free from defects readily visible to the unaided eye. conditions of storage and use, they are suitable for lacquering and printing over the whole surface of the sheet.
NOTE Normally this quality is not available.

2.5.3.2 Second grade - Seconds is the grade designation given electrolytic tinplates which at the time of despatch have a minimum 75 percent of usable area.

2.5.3.3 Unassorted grade ( standard ) - Unassorted ( UA ) is the grade designation given to electrolytic tinplates, normally produced in line These contain using usual inspection and classification procedures. primes and seconds. The quantity of seconds may be up to 15 percent at the time of despatch. 2.5.4 Menders - Hot dipped or electrolytic for surface blemishes, which can be repaired in the hot-dipping process. tinplate, initially rejected or made good by retinning

2.5.5 Unmended Menders - Electrolytic menders which have not been repaired by hot-dipped tinning. They have superficial defects mainly affecting the surface appearance, but they conform to the specified tin coating weight.

Waste- Waste

2.5.6.1 Assorted waste-waste ( hot dipped and electrolytic ) - Tinplate which at the time of despatch may have visible imperfections of moderate and is supplied assorted to size, gauge, tin magnitude or frequency, coating and temper. 2.5.6.2 Unassorted waste-waste ( hot dipped and electrolytic ) - Tinplate which at the time of despatch may have visible imperfections of moderate supplied in mixed Th is material is generally magnitude or frequency. sizes, tempers and thickness and may be off the tolerance in tin coating masses and can be a mixture of bright, matt or stone finish. 2.5.7 Mill Excess or Mill Over Runs - These are tinplates of standard grade ( unassorted grade ) accumulating in the mills as a result of production having exceeded specific order, calcellation of orders, etc, and supplied assorted in terms of size, gauge and temper. 2.6 Packages and Unit of Trading

2.6.1 Bulk Package ( Sometimes Erroneously Teimed `Stillage' ) - Pack or multiple packing unit comprising stillage, tinplate and packaging material for the shipping of tinplate. 2.6.2 Standard Unit Area of Tinplate metres of tinplate is equal to one SITA Area ). ( SITA ) - Area of 100 square ( System International Tinplate base and

2.6.3 Stillage ( Sometimes Erroneously Termed `Bulk' ) - Wooden platform on which tinplate sheets are stocked to facilitate packing ready transportation. 2.6.4 2.7 Unit ( Packaging ) Terms 100 sheets of given dimensions.

Miscellaneous

2.7.1 List Edge ( or Drip ) - The trailing edge of the sheet during Due to the effect oftin flow passage through the hot-dip tinning bath. and surface tension, the plate, on emergence from the molten tin, carries a thicker tin coating at this edge. Generally the list-edge is deemed to start at the point where the thickness of the sheet has increased by 0.10 mm. 2.7.2 Rolling direction. 2.7.3 Shear direction, Width The dimension The at right angles to the rolling to the rolling

2.7.5 Temper - Summarizing a combination of interrelated mechanical properties. In practice an arbitrary number is used to designate a specified Rockwell 30 T hardness range: which gives a guide to the fabricating properties of the plate. 2.7.6 Tinplate Strips - In coated low carbon steel sheets in which the length is many times the breadth. These are essentiahy cuttings/arisings from unassorted and assorted waste waste quality .tinplate and are generally sold without specifications excepting for the range of thickness and dimensions.
